thesis_text:
Bottom line: for Bain & Company (Consulting, entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-10-12 with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. Stated bar: strong academics, analytical and communication skills, and a demonstrated record of initiative, leadership and teamwork, open to every discipline. The process then tests structured problem solving directly through an online assessment and case interviews. No GPA cutoff is published on the official pages checked.

Who gets in (sample N=not available — curated-qualitative record, as of 2026-10-12):
- This CIR is curated-qualitative: no population sample exists for it yet, so there are no percentages to show. What follows is the reported pattern from public sources, labeled as such.
Known biases of this data: Deadline evidence mixes official Bain school pages with one university career center notice; the October date should be re-confirmed on an official page at application time.; Process detail (assessment vendor, two case rounds, November timing) is drawn from Bain's official London page and may differ in US offices.; No population data - stated eligibility (all disciplines) is not evidence about who is actually hired.. We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).

What Bain & Company says it screens for vs what the record shows:
Stated: Online assessment after application covering numerical aptitude, logical reasoning and behavioural preferences (Sova), per the official London recruiting page. Strong academic background, analytical skills, high motivation and outstanding interpersonal skills on the official ACI page.
Revealed: 

Routes in, ranked for you:
First: Associate Consultant (full-time), US — Full-time deadline October 11, 2026, 11:59pm PT; eligible: seniors graduating December 2026-June 2027 and recent graduates within two years of graduation, for Q1 and Summer 2027 cohorts.
Second: Associate Consultant Intern, US — Apply by August 31, 2026 for undergraduates graduating between December 2027 and June 2028.
Third: Associate Consultant, London (non-US, for process contrast) — London page: applications for the Associate Consultant role close October 15 at 23:59 BST, followed by an online assessment and two rounds of case interviews in November to early December.

- school: you — not on file | cohort — See the school pattern in this CIR — stated qualitatively unless the CIR is population-backed; school is not in the user's control, so the plan routes around it (§3.1). | gap | fix: Do not plan around changing schools; offset with experience, projects and referrals.
- experience: you — no internships yet | cohort — Stated bar: strong academics, analytical and communication skills, and a demonstrated record of initiative, leadership and teamwork, open to every discipline. The process then tests structured problem solving directly through an online assessment and case interviews. No GPA cutoff is published on the official pages checked. | gap | fix: Land one real internship or role at a smaller, reachable employer first — the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns.
- projects: you — no projects on file | cohort — Revealed screen in this CIR: evidence of building or analyzing real things (see screening_signals.revealed). | gap | fix: Ship one project that solves a messy real problem for a real user, and document it.
- skills: you — no skills on file | cohort — not on file | unknown
- timing: you — year not on file | cohort — Fall-centred undergraduate cycle with deadlines that have moved into summer: in the 2026 cycle the US full-time first deadline was July 19, the intern deadline August 31, and a further full-time deadline October 11, with interviews following in the fall. | unknown
- authorization: you — not on file | cohort — Sponsorship history is a matter of public record (DOL H-1B LCA filings); this CIR states only what its sources support, and immigration specifics go to the school's international office (§4.8 Q26 — not legal advice). | gap | fix: Confirm sponsorship for this exact role family before investing a season of prep; target employers with a filing history for the role.

The plan:
Next thirty days:
- Confirm this cycle's application window and deadlines for Bain & Company on the official careers page — dates move, and this CIR's cadence fact is the starting point, not the truth (§3.3). (by 2026-10-19)
- Apply to a first, reachable rung: a smaller employer in the same role family (the ladder pattern in this CIR's path patterns). Volume plus follow-up is the play. (by 2026-10-26)
- Ship the first version of one real project and write it up publicly. (by 2026-11-11)
- Build the coffee-chat target list from this CIR's entry routes: recent hires in the same role family, alumni of your school, people one rung up the ladder. (by 2026-10-22)
This semester:
- Convert the semester into signal: one internship or substantial project, one visible leadership or club role in the field, and interview reps on a weekly schedule.
- Run the coffee-chat list: short, specific asks; every conversation ends with a follow-up you actually send.
This year:
- Be in the application pool for Bain & Company's main entry window with the ladder rung, the project write-up and the referral conversations already done — not started.
- If the direct route misses, take the highest adjacent rung this CIR names and re-aim with a year of signal (the risks-and-alternatives route in this thesis).

Coffee-chat strategy: target the profile types named in the ranked routes — recent hires in this role family, alumni of your school now inside, and people one rung up the ladder you are climbing. Ask what the interviews actually test, what surprised them after starting, and what they would do with a semester to prepare. Keep asks short and specific; send the follow-up you promised.

(as of 2026-10-12; recruiting dates shift every cycle — re-check the official careers page before acting, §3.3).

Adjacent options with similar signal: the other employers and role families whose CIRs share this ladder — the first rung matters more than the logo on it.
